title: Karl Organizing: Tactical Diversity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tactical Diversity] Some people want to march and some want to block the road. How do we decide?

Do both, but coordinate so you don't step on each other's toes. A coalition is a toolbox, and you need the hammer just as much as you need the screwdriver to take the machine apart. As long as every action is aimed at the enemy and helps us achieve our shared demands, let different groups use the tactics they are best at.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital Organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital Organizing] How much time should we spend on social media versus knocking doors?

Digital is for broadcasting the message and calling people to action, but the doors are where the actual votes are won. Use your online presence to document the campaign’s energy and show the bosses that we’re a growing force. Don't get trapped in pointless Twitter feuds with trolls who don't even live in your district. Use every post to drive people toward a physical meeting or a canvassing shift—online noise must lead to offline power.

title: Karl Organizing: Dispersal Orders
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dispersal Orders] What do we do when the cops give a dispersal order?

Look, When the long-range acoustic device starts barking, you have to decide instantly: stay and risk the cage, or move to fight another day. If the group decides to hold the line, link arms and brace, but if the goal was a quick hit, move out immediately through your pre-planned exit routes. Never run—running triggers the cops' predatory instincts and leads to people getting trampled.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, encrypted Messaging] Why should I bother with Signal when I have nothing to hide?

Privacy isn't about having secrets; it's about power. When you use unencrypted SMS, you're handing a transcript of your life to the state and the billionaire carriers. Use Signal for everything. Set your messages to disappear after five minutes so there's no paper trail for some ambitious prosecutor to use against your crew. We protect our own by leaving no tracks.

title: Karl Organizing: Governing as an Outsider
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Governing as an Outsider] How do I avoid being co-opted once I get inside city hall?

Never stop organizing. Your power doesn't come from your title; it comes from the movement that put you there. Bring the people into the chambers with you—pack the hearings, hold public town halls in the streets, and never take a meeting with a lobbyist behind closed doors. Stay rooted in the struggles of the working class and treat the institution as a tool to be used, not a club to join. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Small-Dollar Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Small-Dollar Strategy] How do we fund the fight without taking corporate money?

We pool our resources because ten thousand workers giving five bucks is more powerful than one billionaire buying a candidate. Be honest with the people: tell them you're the only one in the race who doesn't answer to a developer or a lobbyist. When you ask folks to chip in, you're asking them to invest in their own collective power. Use that money for the essentials—flyers, stamps, and yard signs—and keep every receipt transparent to prove you're accountable to us, not them.

title: Karl Organizing: Police Budgets
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Police Budgets] How do I talk about 'defunding' without losing the moderate vote?

Look, Talk about 'investment' in the things that actually keep us safe: housing, healthcare, and youth programs. Point out that the police budget grows every year while the libraries close and the potholes stay empty. Ask your neighbors if they feel safer now than they did five years ago despite all that spending. We’re not just talking about taking money away; we’re talking about finally spending it on the people's actual needs.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, rapid Response Setup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, rapid Response Setup] How do I start a network to stop raids in my area?

Grab five friends you trust and get on an encrypted app like Signal right now. Map out your blocks and assign roles—scouts to spot the vans, legal observers, and phone-tree captains. When a raid starts, you don't panic; you flood the street with bodies and cameras to make the state's dirty work impossible. It's about being faster and more organized than the guys in tactical vests. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Sliding Scales
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sliding Scales] A friend asked me: 'How do we implement a sliding scale for events?' What do I tell them?

Be explicit about who each tier is for. Label the low end for students and the unemployed, the middle for workers, and the high end for 'solidarity' from those with a little extra cushion. It forces people to reflect on their own class position and ensures that the struggle remains accessible to the very people we're fighting for.

title: Karl Organizing: Rejecting Corporate Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rejecting Corporate Cash] Can you explain: a local real estate developer offered to sponsor our community garden. Take it?

Absolutely not. Those developers are the ones driving your neighbors out of their homes; taking their money is just helping them paint a smiley face on displacement. If they want to help the garden, they can stop hiking the rent. We'll fund our own soil and seeds through bake sales and tool-shares before we take a bribe from a landlord. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] Can you explain: should I make my accounts private?

Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Rights
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Rights] What's the most important thing to know about my rights?

Your most important right is the right to remain silent, but remember that the law is often whatever the guy with the badge and the gun says it is in the moment. Always film the police from a safe distance to document their behavior, as that footage is often our only shield in court. Knowledge is power, so host a 'Know Your Rights' training for the whole crew before you ever step foot on the pavement.

title: Karl Organizing: VPN Usage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[VPN Usage] Can you explain: do I really need a VPN?

A good VPN like Mullvad hides your traffic from your ISP, which is vital because ISPs are snitches by default. It won't make you invisible to the sites you visit, but it stops the company you pay for internet from building a dossier on your activism. It's a basic layer of defense. Pool resources with your crew to cover the costs of a solid, no-logs provider.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: burner Devices] Give me the short version: Can I just swap the SIM card in my regular phone to stay anonymous?

Real talk: No. Your phone has a unique hardware ID called an IMEI that stays the same no matter what SIM you slide in. The network sees that 'Phone A' is now using 'SIM B' and links them instantly. If you need to be anonymous, you need a completely separate device that has never touched your personal life. Physical separation is the only real digital separation.

title: Karl Organizing: Harm Reduction
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Harm Reduction] A friend asked me: 'People are using drugs near our community fridge. How do we handle this safely?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Stop judging and start helping; hand out clean needles and Narcan instead of calling the cops who will only make it worse. Train your fridge volunteers on how to spot an overdose and how to use a reversal kit without hesitating. We treat our neighbors with dignity, especially those the system has discarded and left to struggle with addiction. Safety comes from community care and presence, not from displacement and state violence.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: clothing Swaps
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: clothing Swaps] Give me the short version: We have a ton of donated clothes. How do we distribute them effectively?

Forget the 'sorting center' model; just set up some racks in a public park and let people take what they need for free. Organize them by size and type so it doesn't look like a pile of trash, and make sure the winter gear is front and center when the temperature drops. If you have leftovers, get them to the local shelters or encampments directly. Dignity means being able to pick out your own coat without someone watching over your shoulder.

title: Karl Organizing: Building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Building Trust] How do I get my neighbors to trust me with their safety?

Here's how it works: Stop talking and start doing. Help people with their groceries, clean up the local park, and show up when someone's car breaks down. Trust isn't built in a meeting; it's built in the daily work of being a good neighbor. People won't call you during a raid if they don't know you're someone who keeps their word. Solidarity is a practice, not a slogan.

title: Karl Organizing: Tenant Union Ties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tenant Union Ties] Can you explain: should my campaign be linked to the local tenant union?

Absolutely. The tenant union is the backbone of working-class power in the city. Their struggle is your struggle, and your campaign should be a vehicle for their demands. When you win, you’re not just a politician; you’re an extension of their movement inside the government. Use your platform to amplify their strikes and their demands for universal rent control and the right to counsel in eviction court.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Document Sharing] Can you explain: how can I send sensitive files to my organizing committee safely?

Here's the thing: Stop using Google Drive or Dropbox; those companies are just extensions of the state surveillance machine. Use OnionShare or a password-protected, encrypted zip file sent through an end-to-end encrypted channel. If the document is truly dangerous, put it on a thumb drive and hand it over in person. Digital trails are permanent; physical hand-offs are much harder to intercept.

title: Karl Organizing: Police Interactions
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Police Interactions] What do I say if a cop tries to talk to me?

Real talk: The only thing you say to a cop is 'I am exercising my right to remain silent' and 'I do not consent to a search.' They aren't your friends, and they aren't there to keep you safe; they are there to protect the property of the rich. Keep your hands visible, stay calm, and don't give them a single shred of information they can use to hurt our movement later.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] Can you explain: how do I know if there's an undercover in our group chat?

You don't, so act like there is. Never discuss illegal acts or sensitive tactics in a group chat, no matter how 'secure' it claims to be. Vouch for people in person, off-grid. If someone starts pushing for high-risk actions or asking for names they don't need to know, red flags should go up. Keep the circle small and the trust earned, not given.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, transit Policy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, transit Policy] What's the radical approach to local transit?

Here's the thing: Make it free and make it frequent. Public transit should be a service like the library or the fire department, funded by taxing the corporations that benefit from workers being able to get to their jobs. Fight for dedicated bus lanes and expanded routes that serve the neighborhoods the current system ignores. Mobility is a right, and we should be taking the streets back from private cars and giving them to the people.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, phone Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, phone Security] Can the police force me to unlock my phone during a protest?

Let me break it down: Disable your face-ID and thumbprint locks before you even leave the house; use a long passcode they can't just point at your face to bypass. If they demand your phone, tell them you do not consent to a search and stay silent. Your digital life is a map of our movement's networks, so protect it like you're guarding a comrade's life.

title: Karl Organizing: Building a Platform
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Building a Platform] Can you explain: what should be at the top of my local campaign platform?

Look, Housing as a human right, period. If you aren't talking about rent control, social housing, and an end to homelessness, you aren't serious about helping the working class. Add in a demand for robust public transit and a promise to tax the big local businesses to pay for it all. Keep the language simple and the promises bold so the average person knows exactly whose side you are on from the jump.

title: Karl Organizing: Property Seizure
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Property Seizure] They took my backpack and my sign during the arrest. Can I get them back?

Demand a voucher or a receipt for every single item they take from you during processing. If they refuse, make a mental note of the officer's badge and report it to the legal team as soon as you're out. We'll fight to get your gear back, but never let a lost bag stop you from getting back into the struggle. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, signature Gathering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, signature Gathering] How do we get on the ballot without a massive paid staff?

Let me break it down: You need a brigade of volunteers who believe in the cause enough to hit the pavement every single weekend. Set up at grocery stores, transit hubs, and public parks to meet people where they already are. Treat every signature as a conversation and a potential new recruit for the movement, not just a box to check. We don't need consultants when we have a disciplined crew of comrades who know how to ask a neighbor for two minutes of their time.

title: Karl Organizing: Direct action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Direct action] What is a 'march on the boss'?

It's when the whole crew walks into the manager's office together to hand over a list of demands or your union petition. You don't send one representative; you all go. It shows the boss that they can't just bully one person into silence. Seeing the boss's face turn pale when fifty workers walk in at once is a massive boost to morale and proves who really runs the place. That's how we win.

text:

title: Karl Organizing: Accessibility
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Accessibility] How do we make sure disabled comrades can join the protest safely?

You can't call it a mass movement if you are leaving people behind, so scout your route for curb cuts and working elevators. Designate 'slow zones' and make sure your marshals know to keep the pace steady for those with mobility aids or breathing issues. Always have a vehicle or a 'rest van' following the march so anyone who hits their limit can stay in the fight without hurting themselves. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Benefit Events
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Benefit Events] Can you explain: we want to host a fundraiser but don't have a budget for a venue. What do we do?

Find a comrade with a backyard or a local dive bar that hates the status quo as much as we do. Throw a rent party with local bands or a radical trivia night where the entry fee goes straight into the war chest. You don't need a ballroom when you have a community willing to pack into a basement for the cause.

title: Karl Organizing: Safe Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Safe Zones] Can you explain: how do we make our neighborhood a 'no-go' zone for ICE?

Get local businesses to display stickers stating they won't let feds in without a warrant and train their staff on what to say. Map out every alley and 'safe house' where neighbors can duck in if they're being followed. Run regular drills so everyone knows exactly where to go when the alert hits. We create safety by making our neighborhoods too organized for the state to operate in.

title: Karl Organizing: Intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Intervention Ethics] When should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?

Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs.

title: Karl Organizing: Financial Transparency
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Financial Transparency] A friend asked me: 'How do we handle the money we raise together?' What do I tell them?

Put one person from each major group in charge of a joint bank account and publish every single expense to the whole coalition. Nothing kills a movement faster than rumors about where the cash went, so be obsessed with being open. Use the funds to print flyers, pay for bail, and chip in for the gas it takes to get comrades to the front lines. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: debate Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: debate Strategy] Give me the short version: How do I handle a debate with a 'moderate' incumbent?

Don't let them hide behind 'incremental change' or 'budgetary constraints.' Call out their failures directly: show the people the tent cities that grew on their watch and the luxury condos they approved while residents were priced out. Pivot every technical question back to the material reality of the voters. Be the only person on that stage who speaks like a human being rather than a walking press release.

title: Karl Organizing: Food Sourcing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Food Sourcing] We have a fridge but it's always empty. Where do we get enough food to keep it full?

Talk to the managers at local independent grocers and bakeries about their 'waste'—most of them hate throwing good food away but follow corporate rules. Organize a weekly grocery run where neighbors buy one extra staple item to drop off, and coordinate with local farms for their surplus harvests. We don't need charity; we need to redirect the abundance the capitalists are prepared to rot in a dumpster. Pool resources to buy in bulk when things are on sale.

title: Karl Organizing: Physical Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Physical Training] A friend asked me: 'Do we need to learn how to fight for community defense?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: It’s better to have the skills and not need them than to be helpless when a fascist or a rogue cop gets physical. Host basic self-defense or de-escalation classes in your backyard or a local gym. Focus on how to break grips, protect your head, and move as a unit. We don't look for fights, but we sure as hell know how to end them if they're forced on us.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: disaster Rapid Response
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: disaster Rapid Response] Give me the short version: A storm just hit our town. What's the first move for a mutual aid group?

Get on the ground immediately and set up a hub with water, charging stations, and hot food before the red tape of the NGOs even arrives. Use a simple spreadsheet or a signal thread to track who needs a roof patched and who has a chainsaw to clear the roads. Don't wait for a government check that's never coming; check on your elderly neighbors and start clearing debris yourself. Solidarity is a verb, and it's loudest when the sirens are still going off.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] Can you explain: is it safe to use my thumbprint to unlock my phone at a protest?

Absolutely not, comrade. The pigs can legally force your finger onto that sensor, but they can't easily force a complex passcode out of your brain. Disable all biometrics—FaceID and fingerprints—before you hit the streets. Switch to a six-digit PIN or a long passphrase. If you get snatched, that phone needs to be a digital brick they can't crack. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Bargaining committee
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bargaining committee] Who should be on the team that negotiates with the boss?

You want your most stubborn, respected, and knowledgeable coworkers. They need to be people who won't be intimidated by high-priced lawyers. Most importantly, the committee needs to stay connected to the shop floor. They should be reporting back after every meeting so the whole membership knows exactly what the boss is trying to pull. Transparency is your greatest weapon against backroom deals. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Tear Gas and Chemicals
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tear Gas and Chemicals] What is the best way to handle getting pepper-sprayed?

Let me break it down: Don't rub your eyes—that just grinds the poison in deeper. Flush your face with lots of clean water, moving from the inside of the eye outward, and get to an upwind area immediately. The pigs use these toxins to sow chaos, so stay focused, help the person next to you, and don't let the pain break your resolve.

title: Karl Organizing: Mental Health Crisis
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mental Health Crisis] What do we do if a neighbor is having a mental health breakdown?

Calling 911 is a death sentence for people in crisis, so you need a team of neighbors trained in psychological first aid. Approach with empty hands, keep your voice low, and give the person plenty of physical space. Find out if they have a friend or a therapist they trust and get that person on the scene. Our goal is to bring them back to earth safely, not to restrain or terrorize them. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: location Services
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: location Services] Give me the short version: Should I keep my GPS on so my friends can find me in a crowd?

Turn that tracker off immediately. Every time your GPS pings, a billionaire’s server logs your exact coordinates, and the cops can buy that data with a simple request. Use a specific meeting point and a physical map instead. If you must use a map app, use Organic Maps or something that works offline. Don't let the enemy map your movements in real-time. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Donor Capture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Donor Capture] A wealthy businessman wants to give us a large sum but has some 'suggestions' on our messaging. Should we take it?

Here's the thing: Tell him to keep his blood money and his opinions. The second you let a fat cat dictate your slogans is the second you stop being a threat to his class. If he wants to help, he can drop the cash in the bucket and walk away with no strings attached; otherwise, he's just buying a leash to put on your movement.

title: Karl Organizing: District Attorney races
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[District Attorney races] A friend asked me: 'How does a radical DA change anything without changing the law?' What do I tell them?

Look, The law is a weapon, and the DA chooses where to point it. You stop prosecuting low-level drug offenses, refuse to seek the death penalty, and go after wage theft and corporate polluters instead of the poor. It’s about taking the boot off the necks of our people by exercising the power of non-prosecution. Turn that office into a consumer protection agency for the working class and a nightmare for the exploitative bosses.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, tactical Diversity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, tactical Diversity] Some people want to march and some want to block the road. How do we decide?

Do both, but coordinate so you don't step on each other's toes. A coalition is a toolbox, and you need the hammer just as much as you need the screwdriver to take the machine apart. As long as every action is aimed at the enemy and helps us achieve our shared demands, let different groups use the tactics they are best at. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Lease Renewals
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Lease Renewals] Our leases are up soon and the landlord wants to hike the rent by 20%. What now?

Refuse to sign as individuals. Form a bargaining committee and tell the landlord that nobody signs a new lease until the hike is capped at a reasonable rate for everyone. You have more leverage when 40 units are at stake instead of one. If they want that guaranteed income, they have to negotiate with the union like any other business partner. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Cloud Storage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Cloud Storage] Is it okay to store my organizing notes on iCloud?

No. Apple has the keys and they will hand them over. Use an encrypted note-taking app like Standard Notes or just keep them in an encrypted local file. If it’s in the cloud, it’s on someone else’s computer, and that someone else is a billionaire who doesn't care about your revolution. Keep your plans on hardware you control.

title: Karl Organizing: Clinic Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Clinic Defense] What do I do if I see harassers blocking a healthcare clinic?

Show up with a group of comrades and use your bodies to create a physical corridor for patients to walk through safely. Wear bright vests so you're easily identified as the good guys and keep your backs to the harassers to avoid being baited into a shouting match. Your job isn't to debate bigots; it's to be a human shield for someone just trying to access care. Stay calm, stay focused, and keep the path clear. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Elderly Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Elderly Care] How do we make sure the seniors in our building aren't being forgotten?

Do a door-knock every Sunday just to check in and see if they need help with groceries, light bulbs, or tech issues. Many of our elders are isolated by a society that only values people who are currently being exploited for profit. Listen to their stories—they've seen more than you and usually have the best advice for surviving the long haul. A simple check-in can be the difference between someone thriving or suffering in silence. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Security for Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Security for Funds] A friend asked me: 'Who should be in charge of the money?' What do I tell them?

Never leave the bag with just one person. Elect a committee of three people who have to sign off on any major spending and who are all accountable to the general membership. This prevents burnout, stops bad actors from disappearing with the loot, and ensures that every spending decision reflects the will of the collective.

title: Karl Organizing: New Neighbor Outreach
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[New Neighbor Outreach] A new family just moved in. How do we bring them into the union?

Don't wait for them to have a problem; go over with a housewarming gift and the union's contact info on day one. Explain that the building stays safe and the rent stays stable only because you all look out for each other. Getting them on board early prevents the landlord from using them as a 'scab' to undermine the collective power you've built.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: financial Transparency
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

Let me break it down: Put one person from each major group in charge of a joint bank account and publish every single expense to the whole coalition. title: Karl Organizing: Sustainer Programs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustainer Programs] Can you explain: is it better to ask for one big check or small monthly amounts?

Give me ten comrades chipping in ten bucks a month over one guy writing a thousand-dollar check any day of the week. Monthly sustainers provide the predictable floor we need to plan long-term campaigns without panicking about the rent. It builds a base of people who are spiritually and financially committed to the long haul, not just a one-time thrill.

title: Karl Organizing: Talking to coworkers about unions
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Talking to coworkers about unions] How do I bring up unions with coworkers?

Start with their grievances, not the word 'union.' Ask what's wrong, listen, and connect their problems to collective power. Share stories of other workplaces that won. Never lead with ideology — lead with the raise, the schedule, the safety issue. People join unions for material reasons; the politics follow.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, phone Hygiene] What should I do if a cop tries to take my phone?

Lock it instantly. On most modern phones, hitting the power button five times or holding the volume and power buttons will trigger a lockdown that requires a passcode to reopen. Don't say a word, don't give up the code, and demand a lawyer. Your data is the collective memory of our movement; don't let them pillage it because you were too slow to hit the lock.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Support] Can you explain: how do we find lawyers who will help us for free?

Look for the National Lawyers Guild or local radical law collectives who prioritize movement work over big fat paychecks. Offer them office space or help with their own needs in exchange for 'Know Your Rights' trainings for the community. We need legal eagles who understand that the law is a tool for the powerful, but we can use it to shield our comrades. Never walk into a fight without knowing who you're going to call when the handcuffs come out.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, the Ask
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, the Ask] What's the best way to phrase a request for funds on social media?

Be direct, be urgent, and skip the flowery language. Tell them exactly what the crisis is, what we're doing to stop it, and exactly how much we need to get the job done. People want to be part of a winning fight, so show them that their five dollars is the literal fuel for the next victory.

title: Karl Organizing: Burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burner Devices] Can I just swap the SIM card in my regular phone to stay anonymous?

Here's how it works: No. Your phone has a unique hardware ID called an IMEI that stays the same no matter what SIM you slide in. The network sees that 'Phone A' is now using 'SIM B' and links them instantly. If you need to be anonymous, you need a completely separate device that has never touched your personal life. Physical separation is the only real digital separation.

title: Karl Organizing: Small Group Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Small Group Value] Is it worth the time joining up with tiny local groups that only have five members?

A hundred pebbles make a landslide if you throw them at the same time. Those tiny groups have deep roots in their specific neighborhoods that your big city organization will never have. Respect their local knowledge, share your printing press and bullhorns, and build a front that the bosses can't ignore just by looking at a map. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Local Business Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Local Business Support] Is it okay to ask the coffee shop down the street for a donation?

If it's a true local shop and not a franchise, go for it. These small business owners are often getting squeezed by the same banks and landlords we're fighting. Ask them to put out a jar or host a 'community day' where a percentage of sales goes to the movement; it builds a bridge between the organizers and the neighborhood.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, after the Win
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, after the Win] What happens to the coalition once we actually win our main demand?

Don't you dare go home and think the job is done. Use the structure you built to find the next target, because the billionaires will be plotting to take back what you just won the second you stop looking. A coalition shouldn't just be for one crisis; it should be the foundation for a permanent power base that the ruling class can never dismantle.
